headline: UK AISI Puts External Testing at Frontier AI Governance Center
summary: The UK AI Security Institute is pioneering independent cyber-capability testing for advanced AI models like OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and Anthropic's Claude Mythos.
details: The UK AI Security Institute (AISI) is placing external cyber-capability testing at the forefront of frontier AI governance. This approach involves evaluating advanced AI systems, such as OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and Anthropic's Claude Mythos, under controlled conditions that allow evaluators access beyond typical public deployment safeguards.

The core takeaway is not that a single model has crossed a definitive threshold, but rather that pre-deployment external evaluation is emerging as a practical mechanism for assessing frontier models' capabilities in realistic, contained environments. Both Anthropic and OpenAI have confirmed AISI's involvement in testing their respective advanced systems.

AISI's evaluation of Claude Mythos Preview's cyber capabilities, conducted in controlled settings, offers a clear official account. Anthropic has also stated that its Mythos 5 models will undergo external testing with UK AISI as part of its trusted-access Project Glasswing program. OpenAI's GPT-5.6 System Card indicates that UK AISI received early access to GPT-5.6 Sol for pre-deployment evaluation.

These evaluations are crucial because they allow for the examination of AI systems under conditions relevant to potential risks, rather than solely through the lens of consumer product interactions. Factors like enhanced tools, extended task times, realistic environments, and fewer deployment restrictions can significantly alter a system's capabilities.

The program raises important governance questions, highlighting the value of independent evaluators who can test models in structured conditions and communicate findings to developers and policymakers. This complements existing commitments, policies, and safety reports.

The model-access arrangements are particularly significant. For trusted-access testing, safeguards are sometimes lifted, allowing evaluators to examine systems more thoroughly. This approach underscores the need to evaluate safeguards alongside the system's underlying capabilities, access controls, and intended deployment context.

For organizations developing with advanced AI, safety evaluation should be integrated into implementation planning from the outset. This includes considering AI architecture, workflow design, and access controls for security-sensitive integrations.

A key future policy challenge is ensuring comparability across evaluations. While the current research does not establish a universal benchmark, it clearly demonstrates that independent testing is becoming an integral part of the operating model for frontier AI releases.

headline: Reddit enlists AI to help moderate new subreddits
summary: The platform is rolling out 'Rules Hub,' an LLM-powered tool for automated moderation, ahead of a full launch later this year.
details: Reddit is introducing "Rules Hub," a new suite of moderation tools powered by large language models (LLMs). These tools will help moderators enforce community rules by evaluating whether posts and comments match the intent of a rule, handling nuance and natural language more effectively than traditional keyword matching.

The Rules Hub has been in testing for several months with moderators from over 700 communities. It is now expanding to all newly created communities and is slated for a wider rollout later in 2026. While optional for new communities, Reddit plans to eventually replace many of Automod's enforcement features with Rules Hub.

Beyond moderation, Reddit is also making significant changes for developers. New third-party apps will be required to use Reddit's Developer Platform instead of the API, aligning with the company's strategy to manage data access and ensure consistent policy enforcement.

This shift follows Reddit's controversial API changes in 2023, which aimed to monetize data for AI companies but led to backlash and the shutdown of many third-party apps. Reddit assures ample notice and a clear timeline for this transition.

Reddit is also taking further steps to combat unauthorized content scraping, particularly by AI companies. These efforts include blocking certain search engines and suing companies like Anthropic and Perplexity. Changes are also planned for the "old Reddit" interface, with initial steps including limiting access to logged-in users and migrating critical bots and moderator workflows.
